title: INFLAMeR machine learning predicts functional lncRNAs, including SNHG6 in leukemia
summary: INFLAMeR, a model using 71 genetic features, was trained on CRISPR interference screens across seven cell lines to predict functional lncRNAs. Cell-based and transcriptomic validation of nearly fifty genes in K562 cells found cell type-specific function for 85% of predicted lncRNAs. SNHG6 knockdown reduced leukemia cell proliferation and, per the abstract, affected drug response and differentiation, and a mouse K562 xenograft model was used to test tumor growth in vivo.
ai_technology: INFLAMeR, a machine learning model using transcription factor binding and other genetic features

evidence.tested: Knockdown of candidate lncRNAs in K562 cells, transcriptomics, drug-response assays and a mouse xenograft for SNHG6.
evidence.unknown: Whether candidates work outside K562 cells and in patients; part of the abstract on SNHG6 results was truncated; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Prioritizes lncRNAs likely to be functional, which were then tested experimentally.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
